question: A, B, and C together can complete a task in 6 days. If A alone takes 12 days and B alone takes 18 days, how long will C alone take?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM of 6, 12, 18 = 36 units.

Combined efficiency of A, B and C = 36 ÷ 6 = 6 units/day.

Efficiency of A = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day, Efficiency of B = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day.

Efficiency of C = Total efficiency − (A + B) = 6 − (3 + 2) = 1 unit/day.

Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 6 days

Time taken by A alone = 12 days

Time taken by B alone = 18 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of C = (Combined efficiency of A, B, C) − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 6 − (3 + 2) = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time required by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time required by C alone = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 days

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Follows the exact same LCM logic as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, and outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed strictly in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If all work together for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, find the total work done in a full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply it to reach close to the total work, then add the remaining days individually.
